_what: Declarative watch list for the ternary-leg watchdog (.github/workflows/ternary-leg-watchdog.yml).
_why: Monitoring used to live in a background poller inside an agent session. That dies whenever the session or container stops -- twice on 2026-07-25, once silently for 31 minutes on an unbounded curl -- and a long GPU leg then runs unwatched: a spot preemption is not noticed, nothing resumes it, and the wall clock is lost. This file plus the scheduled workflow move the watch OUT of the session entirely. All state lives in the repo and in GCS, so it survives restarts, and no agent needs to be awake.
_how: The workflow runs on a cron. For each enabled entry it asks GCS three questions: is the leg's result JSON already there (done), is the leg ADVANCING (a live VM whose committed iteration is still climbing), or is it dead/stalled? Only a dead leg is re-dispatched, which resumes from the last committed checkpoint. A per-day relaunch counter in GCS caps runaway re-dispatch, and every outcome is an annotation; a stall or a hit cap also FAILS the job so GitHub's own failure notification fires.
_editing: Set enabled=false when a leg is finished or deliberately parked -- do NOT delete the entry, so the history of what was watched stays legible. The watchdog is a no-op with an empty or all-disabled list.
_required_keys_are_enforced: ONE FACT, ONE PLACE: `_required_run_params` is the single authoritative list and `_required_run_params_note` explains it. `_prefix_keying_params` is retained ONLY as a backward-compatible alias, because a copy of watchdog_validate.py held by another session may still read that key; it is a SUBSET (it lacks use_preequil) and must not be treated as the requirement. The workflow validates the list on every pass and refuses to act on an incomplete entry rather than relaunching the wrong thing.

watch.note: valB_mini reverse leg — the preregistered |dG_fwd + dG_rev| antisymmetry check, still null on all three legs. Its result decides whether the r0 systematic sits in the model/reference data (rescope the calibrator) or in interface substates (change the rescope design first). use_preequil=1 IS THE FIX AND IS ALSO WHAT FWD DID. nr4a3_ternary_fep.py records it verbatim: 'The fix that WORKS is NOT a smaller timestep: relax the fully-interacting physical complex with plain MD BEFORE the alchemy ... where every prior run died at warmup iter 1.' Both 2026-07-25 rev attempts died at warmup iter 1 -- at 2.0 fs (state 1) and at 1.0 fs (state 7) -- confirming empirically that the timestep is not the lever. fwd's prefix is ..._wu1.0_v2pe, and that salt is named for the v2 PRE-EQUILIBRATED setup (SETUP_VER=v2pe is set only by use_preequil=1), so pre-equilibration is not a deviation from fwd: it is what fwd did, which fixes the crash AND preserves comparability for the hysteresis test.

_required_run_params_note: Every parameter the watchdog must REPRODUCE on a relaunch; `_required_run_params` below is the authoritative list. Two classes, both mandatory. (1) PREFIX-KEYING: the spot commit prefix is <seed>_dt<timestep_fs>fs_clig0_wu<warmup_timestep_fs>[_<commit_salt>][_dir<direction>], so omitting one makes the watchdog resume a DIFFERENT trajectory than the one it is watching. (2) NOT prefix-keying but SYSTEM-CHANGING: use_preequil selects whether the alchemy starts from the plain-MD-relaxed physical complex (SETUP_VER=v2pe) or the raw one (v1). CORRECTED 2026-07-25 -- an earlier version of this note claimed pre-equilibration 'only moves coordinates' so 'the particle counts are IDENTICAL' and OpenFE could not catch a v1/v2pe cross-restore. That was never measured and it is FALSE: the prime markers give v1 = 146,020 particles and v2pe = 141,968, because the pre-equilibrated complex is RE-SOLVATED, so assert_multistate_system_equality WOULD reject a cross-restore. Reproducing use_preequil is mandatory for a stronger reason: the setup-cache key carries the version (..._r0__nagl__v1 vs ..._r0__nagl__v2pe), so getting it wrong runs a DIFFERENT SYSTEM, not merely a bad resume. That is what happened: four rev attempts ran the 146,020-particle v1 system against a fwd leg built at 141,968, and all four died at warmup iteration 1. See sections J-J.5 of ternary-lane-guard-audit-2026-07-25.md.
_relaunch_cap_note: max_relaunches_per_day was 8 and that is a HARD BLOCKER at the observed spot preemption rate. Measured 2026-07-25: two consecutive L4 spot VMs on this leg lasted ~30 min and <=62 min (mean ~45 min). Against 26.4 h of remaining MD that is ~35 VM lifetimes, so a cap of 8 would stop the watchdog relaunching on day one and the leg would sit dead with no GPU running and only a CAPPED annotation to show it. Raised to 40. RAISING IT IS SAFE ONLY BECAUSE the crash detector now separates the two cases: a leg that DIED (no VM, no post-mortem -- preemption) is relaunched and resumes from its last committed checkpoint, while a leg that CRASHED (post-mortem newer than its VM) is reaped and explicitly NOT relaunched. So a deterministic failure cannot spin the counter; only preemptions consume it, and each one resumes rather than restarts. Before the crash detector existed, a low cap was the only thing standing between a repeating crash and a runaway.
_provisioning_note: spot | standard(=on-demand). Read from config rather than hardcoded in the watchdog, so switching is a one-line edit. THE VALUE IS A HUMAN DECISION: gpu-ternary-fep-gcp.yml states 'Use standard ONLY when explicitly authorized for a time-sensitive one-off, e.g. confirming a single valB leg', so it is not self-authorizing even though the cost is expiring GCP trial credit rather than cash. MEASURED CASE FOR CONSIDERING IT (2026-07-25): spot delivered 96 warmup iterations in 103 min across 2 preemptions and 3 setup cycles = 55.9 iter/h against a theoretical 106.2 iter/h at the measured 33.91 s/iter, i.e. 53% efficiency. The remaining 2704 iterations are ~48 h of calendar on spot vs ~25.5 h un-preempted, a ~23 h difference. Spot also caps max-run at 25200s (7 h) while standard gets 72000s (20 h), so standard means ~2 VM lifetimes instead of ~35. Against that: pricing.md forbids quoting the L4-on-demand figure as a go-forward cost basis, and the standing rule is DEFAULT EVERY GPU RUN TO SPOT.
